row.name: West Ridge Approach
row.overview: The West Ridge approach to Bonanza Peak is longer and more secluded than the North Ridge. It involves more Class 2-3 scrambling with steeper sections and better views of the surrounding mountains. Popular for parties seeking less crowded access.

pitch_detail.notes: Open terrain giving way to rockier ground near the 7,100 ft col.

row.approach: From Holden Village, follow the Railroad Creek Trail roughly 3-3.5 miles to Hart Lake (3,956 ft). From the lake, climb cross-country (no maintained trail) approximately 2.5 hours to the 7,100 ft pass on Bonanza's west ridge, which gives access to the base of the Southwest/West Peak routes.
row.descent_text: Parties finishing routes on the west side (e.g., the Soviet Route) typically descend via talus and short rappels on the northwest side back toward this pass, then retrace the approach down to Hart Lake and the Railroad Creek Trail to Holden Village.
hazards: Volcanic rock stability — loose red/orange rock with poor friction, especially when wet
Steeper pitches — Class 2-3 sections with 30-40 degree angles, higher exposure than North Ridge
Descent route-finding — west ridge descent options are less obvious than return via ascent route
Weather risk — exposed ridge collects afternoon electrical activity
watch_out: Loose volcanic rock — red volcanic rock is notably unstable and slick when wet; test handholds carefully
Exposure increase — steeper than North Ridge with 30-50 ft exposure in places, significant falling risk
Route-finding descent — west side offers multiple descent gullies, but wrong choice adds hours; stay oriented
Weather window critical — afternoon thunderstorms more likely on exposed ridge; start early
